beats.say: Cymbal just bought a fashion brand. And it runs on AWS.
Leadership wants one view of all the data.
beats.label: The ask
beats.head: One view of all the data

beats.say: But customer data from Europe has to stay in Europe.
beats.label: The catch
beats.head: EU data stays in the EU

beats.say: Two ideas solve this. Keep things portable, and make data easy to find.
beats.label: Station 1.3 · Flexibility and portability
beats.head: Portable, and easy to find

beats.say: Idea one: do not lock yourself in.
Think of a power plug adapter. The same device works in any country.
beats.label: Think of an adapter
beats.head: One device, any socket

beats.say: Apache Beam is like that for pipelines. The same code runs on Dataflow, Flink or Spark.
beats.label: Portable pipelines
beats.head: Apache Beam

beats.say: Dataproc runs your open source Spark and Hadoop jobs with no changes.
beats.label: Portable jobs
beats.head: Dataproc

beats.say: And open formats, like Iceberg and Parquet, keep your data readable by any engine.
beats.label: Portable data
beats.head: Open formats: Iceberg, Parquet

check.prompt: Data in AWS must stay in AWS. Analysts want to query it from BigQuery. What do you use?
check.why: BigQuery Omni runs the query inside AWS. The other two copy the data out.

beats.say: Now the hard part. The data in AWS must not move.
So do not move the data. Move the query.
beats.label: The answer
beats.head: Move the query, not the data

beats.say: BigQuery Omni runs your query inside AWS or Azure. Only the results come back.
beats.label: BigQuery Omni
beats.head: Runs the query inside AWS or Azure

beats.say: BigLake adds table security on top of plain files: rows and columns, like a warehouse.
beats.label: BigLake
beats.head: Warehouse security over plain files

beats.say: The trap is copying S3 data into Google Cloud when it must stay in AWS.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Copying S3 data out when it must stay in AWS

check.prompt: Before you change a column, you want to see what is built from it. Which feature shows that?
check.why: Lineage shows the tables and jobs downstream of a table.

beats.say: Idea two: data nobody can find might as well not exist.
Dataplex organizes data without moving it. Think of it as a map of your data.
beats.label: Dataplex
beats.head: Organizes data without moving it

beats.say: A lake is a domain, like Sales. A zone is raw or curated. An asset is a bucket or a dataset.
beats.label: The Dataplex words

beats.say: The catalog is the search box. It collects metadata on its own, so people can search.
beats.label: Knowledge Catalog
beats.head: A search box for all your data

beats.say: And lineage shows what feeds what. Check it before you change a column.
beats.label: Data lineage
beats.head: See what feeds what

beats.say: The trap: building your own metadata database. A managed catalog already exists.
beats.label: Exam trap

beats.say: Recap.
Keep compute portable with Beam and Spark. Keep data open. And when data cannot move, query it in place.
beats.label: Station 1.3 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Then organize with Dataplex, search with the catalog, and track lineage.
beats.label: Station 1.3 · 2 of 2

beats.say: Your turn. Try the checkpoint below.
